**ANTHONY, 2026-08-14, ON HIS WORK COMPUTER, JUST AFTER UPDATING: `● Unknown command: /capture-session`. THE SKILL EXISTS, IS SERVED, AND HAS NO COMMAND — AND THE ONE PLACE THAT CANNOT REPRODUCE THIS IS THE REPO WHERE THE DECISION WAS MADE.**

═══ MEASURED, 2026-08-14 ═══
```
getting-started/skills/     20 skills served
getting-started/commands/   11 command files
```
The eleven: `/adopt /brainstorm /debt /decisions /gaps /genesis /health /kpp /req /rules /where`.

Two of them front a TOOL, not a skill — `debt.md` calls `loop_status`, `decisions.md` queries. So **nine commands front a skill, and ELEVEN OF THE TWENTY SKILLS ARE FRONTED BY NOTHING**: capture-session, ci-gate, impact-check, ingest-corpus, link-artifacts, link-projects, parallel-work, plan-increments, report-friction, retire-from-design, revise-design.

⇒ On a consumer install those eleven are reachable only if the agent thinks to call `get_skill`. **`capture-session` is one of them, and it is the skill whose own text says the user should not have to be the trigger.**

═══ ⭐⭐ WHY NOBODY HERE COULD SEE IT ═══

Anthony, correcting this session: *"seems to work here fine, as well as /capture-intent."* **He is right, and the reason is the finding.**
```
.claude/skills/   20 directories   <- the SOURCE the binary compiles in
```
Claude Code loads a project's `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` as `/<name>`. This checkout holds all twenty **as sources**, so in reflow2's own repo every skill resolves as a slash command — including the eleven that ship with none. `/capture-intent` resolves here for that reason and cannot resolve on a consumer install, where nothing is copied (`dec:skills-served`).

**The decision's own question (`question:5aa0248a4e730d34`) asked whether commands should ship "so a consumer project gets the same ergonomics reflow2's own repo has". The repo's ergonomics come from the SKILL SOURCES, not from the commands — so the eleven were never sized against the twenty they were meant to match.** This is `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` arriving in the environment again, the same shape as the symlinked kit in `fact:updating-reflow2-does-not-update-a-project-already-set-up` and found the same day.

═══ 🛑 THE GUARD IS ASYMMETRIC, AND THAT IS WHY IT STAYED QUIET ═══

`dec:commands-are-the-exception` names ONE rot direction and closes it: *"a command could name a skill that no longer exists. `skill_lint` fails on exactly that."* **The opposite direction — a skill that no command names — is checked by nothing.** Grepped `tools/test_init.py` and `tools/skill_lint.py`: no assertion pins the command count or compares the two sets, so every skill added since has shipped uncovered in silence. Nine of the eleven uncovered skills postdate the decision.

═══ 🛑 AND THE RECORD SAYS EIGHT ═══

`dec:commands-are-the-exception`, `chg:commands-ship` and `ver:install-reaches-the-agent` all say **eight** slash commands and enumerate them. **Eleven ship** — `/adopt`, `/genesis` and `/rules` were added without the record moving. Nothing pins the number, so nothing noticed.

═══ ✅ THE OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS SHARPER THAN EITHER HYPOTHESIS ═══

This node previously left open WHY he expected `/capture-session` there, naming two readings: he reached for a skill he knew existed, or the project predates `dec:skills-served` and carried copied skills the update pruned.

**ANTHONY, 2026-08-14: "I believe the project pre-dates the capture-session skill."** MEASURED: capture-session shipped in `4a9f4e7` (PR #163) on **2026-08-12**, released in v0.29.0 the same day.

⇒ **THE PRUNED-COPY READING IS RULED OUT FOR THIS SKILL. A project set up before 2026-08-12 never held a capture-session copy to prune — the skill did not exist when its kit was written.** So the command was never there, was never removed, and could not have resolved at any point in that project's life.

⭐⭐ **WHICH LEAVES THE FIRST READING, AND IT IS A CLEANER DEMONSTRATION OF THE BLIND SPOT THAN THE MEASUREMENT ABOVE.** He knew the skill's NAME — and the place he could have learned it is the reflow2 checkout, where `.claude/skills/capture-session/` makes it a working slash command. **The maintainer learned a skill's name in the one environment where typing it works, then typed it where it never could.** The blind spot is not only that the repo cannot reproduce the defect; it is that the repo actively TEACHES the wrong affordance.

📌 SECOND-ORDER, AND IT COMPOUNDS: a project set up before 2026-08-12 also carries a KIT from before then, so whatever commands it does have are that generation's. `fact:updating-reflow2-does-not-update-a-project-already-set-up` — the binary updates, the per-project kit does not — applies to this machine directly. `reflow2 init . --harness=claude` is what refreshes it; `ls .claude/commands` says whether `init` was ever run there at all.
